transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um... I guess I just don't really feel like myself anymore. I don't know. I just kind of... go flat, and quiet. I barely talk to people lately. Even just being at work... getting started on my cleaning route just feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you been hearing voices that other people do not hear?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes. Mostly just when I'm working late. When I'm mopping after hours, I'll hear... a man's voice. He just says my name, or tells me I missed a spot. It sounds clear, like he's standing right by the stairwell. But... when I look, there's nobody there. So... yeah.
Have you ever heard this voice during a time when you were not feeling depressed or low?

Um... yeah. There was a time... maybe for a few weeks. I was feeling a bit better. I could actually eat a full meal, and getting through my shift wasn't as hard. But... I still heard him. Just... calling my name by the stairs. And... I still knew they were watching me on the hallway cameras. Tracking where I went. So... yeah, it didn't stop just because I felt a little better.
How long have you been hearing the man's voice?
Um... a while, I guess. It's been... maybe about 11 months now. With the voice, and... the cameras. Yeah. About 11 months.
Did the voice and beliefs about the cameras begin while you were using drugs or during a period soon after using them?
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were not depressed, but you still heard the voice or believed the cameras were watching you?

Yeah... I think I said that already. There was a few weeks where I wasn't so low. I was eating... working okay. But the voice in the stairwell didn't stop. And the cameras... I still knew they were tracking me. So, yeah. More than two weeks.
